incident-bot: [ALERT] P1 - sudden surge of 5xx on embeddings-api (/v1/embeddings). paging eng-oncall. pattern: repeated 'kv_spill' + 'disk_throttle' lines in logs. https://observability.redwood/internal/alerts/1901200000 :rotating_light:
neha (eng-sre): Acknowledged. Tom on-call? Can you check autoscaler and filesystem metrics. I'll fetch the spill/runbook steps.
tom (eng-oncall): I'm on it. No deploys in the window. Mount metrics show NVMe write latency spike at 13:42 UTC, queue depth up. Clients hitting long inputs caused large KV cache spills to disk. Turning on ingress throttles for the top 5 noisy client IPs.
jules (platform): I'm disabling KV spill-to-disk in prod (toggle `kv.spill.enabled=false`) to stop the flurry of small writes that are saturating NVMe. Also increasing ephemeral fsync delay to batch writes. Doing change now, will monitor.
neha (eng-sre): Live mitigation: 1) disable kv spill, 2) enable short-circuit fallback-model for requests > 6k tokens, 3) apply per-tenant burst limits for 15m. Apply runbook steps 4b and 4f.
ops-runbook-bot: Executing runbook actions: disable_kv_spill succeeded (run 1901200000-1), set_fallback_threshold seq>6000 succeeded (run 1901200000-2), apply_tenant_burst_limits succeeded (run 1901200000-3).
tom (eng-oncall): After mitigations, 5xx rate dropped ~70% in 8 minutes. Still seeing occasional 504s from queued requests that hit long seq paths. I've set a temporary circuit-breaker on the 'embedding.longseq' pool.
alex (observability): Captured traces. Correlation: KV spill events jump with token count > ~5k, and disk_throttle_ms > 50ms correlates with model request timeouts. Pushing a temporary dashboard tile: "KV spill rate / min" + token-length histogram. Link: https://observability.redwood/dash/1901200000
karen (support): Notified impacted customers (Acct: NovaLabs, ClearHealth). Sending interim message: we've mitigated, ETA for full fix TBD. Will follow up with RCA.
--- resolution ---
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] P1 - traffic stabilized and error rate returned to baseline. Root cause: aggressive KV spill-to-disk writes during a period of many long-sequence embedding requests caused NVMe IO throttling and subsequent model queue timeouts.
neha (eng-sre): Post-incident summary and immediate follow-ups: we need to reduce noisy paging, add deterministic signatures for KV spill/disk_throttle, and tune alert thresholds and suppression logic.
tom (eng-oncall): The page came from a rate-based alert with a 30s evaluation window and no cross-checks. We should: increase eval window to 3m for this rule, require sustained spike AND disk IO saturation before paging, and add a predicate to suppress if `kv.spill.enabled=false`.
jules (platform): We should change autoscale policy to consider 'expected disk write rate' and sequence-length percentiles. Also add a preemptive throttling hook when disk latency crosses 30ms. Filed GH RI-3992 for autoscale changes.
neha (eng-sre): Proposed log-alert update (log-based rule and parser changes):
```
- Query: from logs where service="embeddings-api" and level in ("error","warn") | parse "kv_spill: evicted=(?<evicted>\\d+); throttle_ms=(?<throttle>\\d+)" as evicted, throttle | count by evicted, throttle, bin(1m)
- New signature regex: /kv_spill: evicted=(?<evicted>\\d+); throttle_ms=(?<throttle>\\d+)/ -> tag=kv_spill;alertable=true
- Suppression: only page if (count(evicted>0) > 8 AND avg(throttle) > 40ms) over 5m window
- Eval window: 3m with 1m lookback smoothing
- Add predicate: do not page if `kv.spill.enabled=false` or `fallback_model=true`
```
alex (observability): I'll add the parser signature to the central log pipeline and create a dashboard card: "KV Spill Heatmap (token-length vs throttle_ms)". Also propose a non-paging advisory alert at 3x baseline and paging only at 6x baseline with disk latency condition.
neha (eng-sre): Also we should mute obvious transient disk OOM messages during autoscale ramp to reduce noise. Proposed regex mutes: `/\\b(disk_throttle|ENOSPC|write_timeout)\\b/ -> noise_suppress=true, ttl=15m` and keep a separate high-confidence `kv_spill` signature.
tom (eng-oncall): I'll open the alert-rule PR with the regex and threshold changes. Draft snippet: 
```
# temporary mute for transient disk noise
/\b(disk_throttle|ENOSPC|write_timeout)\b/ -> noise_suppress=true, ttl=15m
# kv_spill actionable signature
/kv_spill: evicted=(\d+); throttle_ms=(\d+)/ -> tag=kv_spill;alertable=true
```
neha (eng-sre): Add metadata to alert payloads: `kv_spill=true/false`, `fallback_enabled=true/false`, `seq_len_bucket=<short|med|long>`, `top_tenants=[...]` so paging contains useful triage signals.
karen (support): For customer comms: please add a short post-incident template with cause, mitigation, and temporary mitigation status. I'll prepare messages for the two affected accounts once we have SR numbers.
jules (platform): ETA on autoscale ticket RI-3992: initial design doc by EOD + spike next sprint. We'll also evaluate persistent NVMe tuning vs. limiting spill behavior.
neha (eng-sre): Action items and owners:
- Alex: add parser signature + dashboards + advisory alert (due EOD)
- Tom: PR for alert regex suppression and threshold changes (due tomorrow morning)
- Jules: autoscale & disk-backpressure ticket (RI-3992) + ETA (due EOD)
- Karen: customer comms draft and SR tracking (due today)
- Neha: update runbook with kv_spill steps & add chaos-suite test for spill behavior (due next week)
ops-runbook-bot: Handoff created to next oncall (tom) with checklist: monitor advisory alert for 8h, escalate if paging resumes.
neha (eng-sre): Thanks team. @tom ping here when PR is merged so we can close the action. :pray:
tom (eng-oncall): PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/alerts/pulls/4899. I set temp suppression rules in staging; will promote to prod after one smoke cycle at 09:15 UTC.
alex (observability): Parser rules and dashboard applied to staging; will push to prod after smoke at 09:00 UTC.
karen (support): Drafted customer note and sent to affected accounts. Closing loop after RCA. :white_check_mark:
